content.title: About
content.content: Low‑moisture part‑skim mozzarella is a semi‑fat cheese made from cow’s milk. It has a firm texture, mild flavor, and excellent meltability, making it a favorite for pizza, baked dishes, and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Low‑moisture mozzarella is preferred for pizza because it melts evenly without releasing excess water.
The part‑skim version contains about 20 % fat, considerably less than traditional mozzarella (around 45 %).
The cheese is produced by pasteurizing milk, then fermenting with rennet to develop curds.
It is sold in blocks, shredded form, or pre‑cut cubes for quick use.
Traditionally mozzarella is formed into balls, but low‑moisture varieties are often molded into blocks.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Mozzarella provides roughly 22 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Calcium is essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Reduced fat content
items.content: Part‑skim mozzarella helps lower overall calorie intake compared with full‑fat cheese.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The cheese is rich in vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Phosphorus
items.content: Phosphorus contributes to energy metabolism and bone health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience digestive discomfort after consuming cheese.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to casein, the main protein in dairy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Mozzarella can contain a notable amount of salt, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Commercial products may include preservatives that are not suitable for all consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Low‑moisture mozzarella is used on pizza, in casseroles, pasta dishes, salads (e.g., Caprese), and as a sandwich filling. It can be cubed, shredded, or torn into pieces. The cheese also melts well in sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store mozzarella in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. After opening, transfer the cheese to a bowl of lightly salted water and change the water every 2‑3 days. It keeps for up to 2 weeks.
